nodes.label: Q11: Service discovery and the service registry
Service registry
nodes.rationale: Services register on startup, heartbeat to keep a lease, and are evicted if they stop answering; addresses cannot live in config because instances change on every deploy, scale event and crash.

nodes.label: Client-side vs server-side discovery
nodes.rationale: Client-side: no extra hop, caller load-balances, every caller needs the registry client. Server-side: simpler callers, one more hop, and the balancer is another thing to run.

nodes.label: It is a lease, not a registration
nodes.rationale: A registry lists what has proved it is running in the last few seconds. Heartbeat at a third of the lease so two can be lost to a blip, and evict with a grace multiplier so a GC pause does not look like a death and make the registry flap. If a heartbeat 404s the service must re-register, not keep heartbeating into a registry that has never heard of it.

nodes.label: Ten-second lookup cache
nodes.rationale: Without a cache the registry sits on the critical path of every call and becomes the least reliable thing in the system. The cost is staleness, which the retry policy absorbs — the cache and the retry policy are designed together — and it makes a registry outage survivable.

nodes.label: Kubernetes makes the registry unnecessary
nodes.rationale: A Service gives a stable DNS name and load balances across pods, and readiness probes play the role of heartbeats — hence Discovery__Enabled: false in the k8s manifest. Building it once by hand is how you learn what the platform does for you.
